newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban reinforce rebels in northern Afghan city.
newsitem.headline: Taleban reinforce rebels in northern Afghan city.

text.p: About 2,500 Islamic Taleban fighters poured into the northern Afghan town of Mazar-i-Sharif on Sunday to reinforce security and impose Islamic Shariah law, one of their commanders said.

Mullah Gul Mohammad, 27, told reporters his Taleban fighters would work alongside the ethnic Uzbek troops of General Abdul Malik, who captured the northern capital from opposition leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum on Saturday.
Malik's tanks and vehicles flew Taleban's white flags when they swept into Mazar-i-Sharif, but only a few Taleban fighters accompanied the initial wave.
"Our plan is first to bring security and Islamic law to Mazar-i-Sharif and then other parts of Afghanistan," said the bearded commander from the northern town of Sar-i-Pul.
Asked if the same strict interpretation of Islam would be enforced in the north as in the Taleban-controlled south, Mohammad said all Afghans must accept Shariah law.
"It would be just like in Kandahar," he said, referring to the austere southern city where Taleban's supreme leader Mullah Mohammad Omar has his headquarters.
